title: Interface Review
description: Per-interface checks for the board's buses and I/O; the reviewer marks whole sections N/A for interfaces the board does not use.

items.text: Differential input voltage is within the PGA gain range for all expected signals
items.hint: Check the worst-case signal including offsets and overrange at the chosen gain; clipping at the PGA output is silent in firmware.

items.text: Common-mode voltage at the PGA inputs is within the specified input common-mode range
items.hint: Many PGAs restrict common-mode range at high gain. Check against the datasheet's CM-vs-gain plot, not just the supply rails.

items.text: Ratiometric measurement is used where appropriate (reference derived from the excitation voltage)
items.hint: Bridges, potentiometers and RTDs cancel excitation drift when the ADC reference tracks the excitation.

items.text: Thermocouple inputs: cold-junction compensation sensor is placed close to the connector junction
items.hint: The CJC sensor must be isothermal with the point where thermocouple wire meets copper. Keep heat sources away from that area.

items.text: RTD / bridge excitation current source value and direction are verified
items.hint: Confirm the compliance voltage is not exceeded at maximum sensor resistance and that self-heating is acceptable.

items.text: Anti-aliasing filter cutoff is well below Nyquist for the chosen sample rate
items.hint: Check the attenuation reached at Fs/2, not just the -3 dB point. Delta-sigma ADCs relax this but still alias around multiples of the modulator rate.

items.text: ADC input impedance is high enough relative to source impedance, or a buffer is added
items.hint: For SAR ADCs, check the sample-capacitor kickback and acquisition time against the source resistance plus the RC filter, per datasheet.

items.text: Reference voltage source meets the stability and noise budget for the required accuracy
items.hint: Compare reference tempco, initial accuracy and noise against the error budget. An internal MCU reference is often the limiting factor.

items.text: Reference pin is decoupled with the capacitance and placement the datasheet specifies
items.hint: Some references go unstable with the wrong capacitor value or ESR. Place the reference cap at the pin, not at the regulator.

items.text: Input overvoltage protection / clamping is present on all ADC inputs that can see out-of-range voltages
items.hint: Use series resistance plus clamps to the rails or TVS. Check that clamp leakage does not create an error at the input impedance used.

items.text: Input mux settling time is budgeted when multiplexed channels are used
items.hint: Switching between channels at very different voltages needs settling time for the RC filter and the sample capacitor.

items.text: Grounding scheme near the ADC follows the datasheet (typically a solid ground with AGND/DGND joined at the converter)
items.hint: Most modern guidance is one unbroken ground plane with careful partitioning, rather than split planes. Confirm digital return currents do not cross the analog area.

items.text: Output voltage range covers the required span for the load
items.hint: Include headroom for the output buffer swing near the rails.

items.text: DAC output buffer / op-amp drive capability is verified for the load impedance
items.hint: Check current drive and stability with the load capacitance, including cable capacitance if the output leaves the board.

items.text: Reference voltage accuracy and noise meet the output accuracy requirement
items.hint: Reference error passes straight to the output. Check its initial accuracy, tempco and noise against the error budget.

items.text: Output reconstruction filter is present where the application needs it and its cutoff is correct
items.hint: Required for waveform / audio generation; usually unnecessary for slow setpoint DACs.

items.text: Settling time meets the system update-rate requirement
items.hint: Use full-scale step settling to the required accuracy, including any buffer and filter.

items.text: DAC output short-circuit / overload protection is considered for outputs that leave the board
items.hint: Series resistance or a protected buffer prevents damage when an external output is shorted.

items.text: DAC output state at power-up and reset is safe for the driven load
items.hint: Many DACs power up at zero-scale or mid-scale. Check what the load does before firmware writes the first code.

items.text: Baud rate, stop bits and parity match between both ends of the link
items.hint: Also check that the clock source gives an acceptable baud-rate error, per the MCU datasheet.

items.text: Logic levels are compatible at both ends, with level translation where supply voltages differ
items.hint: A 5 V TX into a non-5 V-tolerant 3.3 V RX can back-power or damage the receiver.

items.text: RS-232: a transceiver is present and its supply arrangement is per datasheet
items.hint: Modern RS-232 transceivers generate their own bipolar levels with a charge pump; check the pump capacitor values. See also the RS-232 / RS-485 / RS-422 section.

items.text: RS-485: termination (typically 120 Ω) is fitted at each physical cable end only
items.hint: Intermediate nodes must not terminate. See the RS-232 / RS-485 / RS-422 section for further checks.

items.text: RS-485: failsafe biasing holds the bus in a defined idle state
items.hint: Either bias resistors at one node or a transceiver with built-in failsafe. Check the bias still meets the receiver threshold with both terminations fitted.

items.text: RS-485: half-duplex DE/RE control is verified so no bus contention is possible
items.hint: Check DE timing releases after the last stop bit and the default state at MCU reset is receive.

items.text: Flow control (RTS/CTS) is wired if the data rate or latency requires it
items.hint: Without flow control, the receiver must empty its FIFO fast enough at the worst-case interrupt latency.

items.text: ESD protection is fitted on connector pins of externally routed UART lines
items.hint: Choose a TVS whose working voltage clears the signal swing. RS-232 levels need a higher-voltage part than logic-level UART.

items.text: No back-powering occurs through UART lines when one side is unpowered
items.hint: A driven TX into an unpowered device's RX can power it through ESD diodes. Use series resistors, power-off-tolerant buffers or sequencing.

items.text: TX/RX crossover at the connector is documented and matches the cable / mating device
items.hint: TX-to-TX swaps are among the most common respins; label the net names from the MCU's perspective.

items.text: CPOL and CPHA mode is supported by every device on the bus
items.hint: Devices that support different modes on a shared bus force a mode change per transaction. Confirm the firmware handles it.

items.text: CS polarity and setup / hold timing are verified against each device datasheet
items.hint: Some devices need CS toggled between words or a minimum CS-high time between transactions.

items.text: Each device has its own dedicated CS line with no shared-CS conflicts
items.hint: Two devices sharing a CS will contend on MISO. Daisy-chain only where the devices explicitly support it.

items.text: Maximum SPI clock does not exceed any device's rated limit
items.hint: Include the round-trip delay (clock out, data back) for reads at high clock rates.

items.text: Every device tri-states MISO when its CS is de-asserted
items.hint: Some devices (and some ADCs) keep driving MISO; they need a buffer or a separate bus.

items.text: Series source-termination resistors are fitted on long or fast SPI traces to limit ringing
items.hint: Place them at the driver: on SCK/MOSI at the controller, on MISO at each peripheral.

items.text: CS lines have pull-ups so devices stay deselected while the MCU is in reset or unprogrammed
items.hint: A floating CS during boot can let a device clock in noise or drive MISO against another device.

items.text: Pull-up resistor values suit the bus capacitance and clock speed (100 kHz / 400 kHz / 1 MHz)
items.hint: Check rise time against the I2C specification limit for the mode and the sink-current limit at the lowest value.

items.text: Pull-ups are not duplicated across modules or breakout boards in parallel
items.hint: When each module adds its own pull-ups, the effective resistance drops and can exceed the sink-current limit.

items.text: All device addresses on each bus are unique
items.hint: Include reserved addresses and any devices that respond to several addresses.

items.text: Address configuration pins are tied to defined levels, not floating
items.hint: A floating address pin can read differently between units or across temperature.

items.text: Bus capacitance is within budget for the cable / trace length and number of devices
items.hint: Long cables or many devices may need a bus buffer or a slower mode.

items.text: Level shifting is used where devices on the bus run at different supply voltages
items.hint: Use a dedicated I2C level translator or a MOSFET-based shifter. Generic push-pull translators break the open-drain bus.

items.text: A bus-lockup recovery mechanism exists (GPIO to toggle SCL, or a device / bus reset)
items.hint: A device reset mid-transfer can hold SDA low. Firmware recovery clocks SCL until SDA is released.

items.text: No device holds the bus low when it is unpowered while the rest of the bus is powered
items.hint: Devices without power-off-tolerant I/O clamp SDA/SCL through ESD diodes and kill the bus. Check this for every switched rail.

items.text: Externally routed I2C (off-board cable) has ESD protection and is within its capacitance budget
items.hint: I2C is not designed for long cables. Consider a differential extender or a buffer for cable runs.

items.text: Clock roles are assigned so exactly one device drives BCLK and LRCK
items.hint: With two masters the clock lines contend. With no master the codec stays silent.

items.text: BCLK frequency equals sample rate × slot width × number of slots, as verified by calculation
items.hint: Slot width is not always the sample bit depth: 24-bit data in 32-bit slots is common.

items.text: Word-select (WS/LRCK) polarity matches both devices
items.hint: A swapped WS polarity swaps the left and right channels, which is easy to miss in mono testing.

items.text: Data format matches at both ends (I2S, left-justified, right-justified or TDM)
items.hint: A one-bit offset between I2S and left-justified formats halves the amplitude or adds distortion.

items.text: MCLK is provided if the codec requires it and its ratio to the sample rate is supported (e.g. 256 × Fs)
items.hint: Check the codec's supported MCLK/Fs ratios for every sample rate the product uses.

items.text: Codec power-up and mute sequencing avoids audible pops
items.hint: Mute the amplifier until the codec reference has settled, and reverse the order at power-down.

items.text: Series termination resistors are fitted on long I2S traces to reduce ringing
items.hint: Place the resistor at the driver end of each clock line.

items.text: D+ and D− are routed as a length-matched differential pair at 90 Ω differential impedance
items.hint: Matters most at High Speed; Full Speed is tolerant. Use the fab's stack-up to set trace geometry.

items.text: A low-capacitance ESD protection device is fitted on D+ and D− at the connector
items.hint: Choose a part rated for USB data lines (e.g. PRTR5V0U2X class); capacitance limits are tighter at High Speed.

items.text: Pull-up / pull-down on D+ or D− is correct for USB speed and role (host / device / OTG)
items.hint: Many MCUs have integrated pull-ups; an extra external one will break enumeration.

items.text: VBUS has bulk and local decoupling within the limits allowed by the USB specification
items.hint: Device-side VBUS capacitance is limited to control inrush; a host port needs enough bulk to ride through hot-plug events.

items.text: Host / source ports have VBUS current limiting (load switch or polyfuse)
items.hint: Protects the system rail from a shorted cable or a faulty device.

items.text: USB-C CC pins have the correct termination for the role (Rd 5.1 kΩ to GND for sink, Rp for source) or a CC / PD controller for DRP
items.hint: Each CC pin needs its own resistor; sharing one resistor between CC1 and CC2 is a classic failure with e-marked cables.

items.text: Ground reference plane is unbroken beneath the USB differential pair
items.hint: A split or slot under the pair breaks the return path, causing reflections and radiated emissions.

items.text: Connector shield is connected to chassis / GND according to the product's shielding strategy
items.hint: Options include a direct bond, an RC network (e.g. a resistor and capacitor in parallel) or a ferrite. Choose deliberately for EMC and ESD.

items.text: Clock source meets the USB clock tolerance for the chosen speed, per the USB spec and MCU datasheet
items.hint: Crystal-less operation is only valid where the MCU supports clock recovery from SOF packets.

items.text: Device VBUS sensing exists where required and is divided / protected to suit the MCU pin
items.hint: Self-powered devices must not drive D+ pull-up without VBUS present. VBUS pins can see transients above 5 V.

items.text: USB PD: the controller's policy (voltages, currents, dead-battery behavior) is defined and its strapping / firmware matches
items.hint: Dead-battery operation needs the sink to present Rd with no firmware running. Check that the controller supports it.

items.text: USB-C SuperSpeed or alternate-mode lanes have the required AC-coupling capacitors and mux / orientation handling
items.hint: Check capacitor placement and value per the USB spec and the redriver / mux datasheet.

items.text: Suspend current of the bus-powered device is within the USB specification limit
items.hint: Count all leakage paths, LEDs and regulators that stay on in suspend.

items.text: MIPI DSI lane count and data rate match the display module specification
items.hint: Also check the processor's DSI host supports the panel's video or command mode.

items.text: MIPI DSI differential pairs are routed at the specified impedance (typically 100 Ω differential)
items.hint: Set the trace geometry from the fab's stack-up and keep each pair on one reference plane.

items.text: LVDS pairs are length-matched within each pair and between pairs to meet the skew budget
items.hint: Take the skew limit from the LVDS transmitter and panel datasheets.

items.text: Parallel RGB: data, HSYNC, VSYNC and DE are length-matched to PCLK within the timing budget
items.hint: Check setup and hold at the panel against the PCLK edge polarity.

items.text: Display power sequencing (e.g. VDDIO → VDD → backlight) matches the panel datasheet
items.hint: Wrong sequencing can latch up the panel driver IC or show visible artifacts at power-on.

items.text: Backlight PWM dimming frequency avoids visible flicker
items.hint: Rule of thumb: keep it well above a few hundred hertz, and outside the audio band if the inductor or ceramic caps could sing.

items.text: Touch controller bus and interrupt lines are routed with the pull-ups they need
items.hint: See the Touch section for further checks.

items.text: ESD protection is fitted on display connector lines that are user-accessible
items.hint: Keep the ESD device capacitance low enough for the interface speed.

items.text: FPC connector pin-1 orientation, pitch and contact side (top / bottom) match the panel tail
items.hint: A mirrored FPC pinout is a very common respin; check against the panel drawing, not just the netlist.

items.text: Backlight driver has open-LED overvoltage protection
items.hint: If the LED string opens, a boost driver without OVP can exceed its output capacitor and switch ratings.

items.text: Complementary timer outputs have dead time configured to prevent shoot-through
items.hint: Size the dead time from the gate driver and FET switching times, with margin over temperature. See also the Motor Driver Interfaces section.

items.text: Break input (BRK/BRK2) fault wiring is verified for polarity and source
items.hint: The break input should disable the outputs in hardware without needing firmware.

items.text: PWM frequency and resolution meet the application requirement (motor, LED, etc.)
items.hint: Check the timer clock gives the required resolution at the chosen PWM frequency.

items.text: Capture / compare input filters are configured for noise immunity
items.hint: Digital input filters reject short glitches on noisy encoder or capture lines.

items.text: Encoder interface quadrature inputs and index pulse are wired to timer-capable pins
items.hint: Both quadrature channels must land on the same timer's encoder-capable inputs.

items.text: Timer clock source and prescaler values give the required resolution and range
items.hint: Confirm low-power modes or clock-tree changes in firmware do not alter the timer clock unexpectedly.

items.text: Termination (typically 120 Ω) is present at each physical end of the bus only
items.hint: With power off and both ends fitted, CANH to CANL should measure about half the termination value.

items.text: A CAN transceiver sits between the controller TX/RX and the bus CANH/CANL
items.hint: Check the transceiver matches the bus type (high-speed CAN, CAN FD or fault-tolerant).

items.text: Bit rate and sample-point configuration are consistent across all nodes
items.hint: A sample-point mismatch between nodes causes errors on long buses even when the bit rates match.

items.text: Split termination (two half-value resistors with a center-tap capacitor) is used where noise is a concern
items.hint: The center-tap capacitor to ground filters common-mode noise.

items.text: A common-mode choke is fitted on CANH/CANL for EMC-sensitive designs
items.hint: Some chokes can ring with the bus under fault conditions. Follow the transceiver vendor's recommendation.

items.text: ESD / surge protection (TVS) rated for CAN is fitted on CANH and CANL at exposed connectors
items.hint: Use a low-capacitance TVS rated for the CAN bus voltage range.

items.text: Transceiver supports the required data rate (classic CAN or CAN FD) and loop delay
items.hint: Not every transceiver is rated for CAN FD data-phase bit rates.

items.text: Transceiver standby / silent pin has a defined state during MCU reset
items.hint: A floating standby pin can leave the transceiver disabled, or let it disturb the bus during boot.

items.text: Ground reference between nodes is defined (shared ground wire or isolated transceiver)
items.hint: Common-mode range of the transceiver must cover ground offsets between nodes.

items.text: Magnetics (integrated or discrete) are present between PHY and connector
items.hint: Unless the design deliberately uses a capacitively coupled board-to-board link per the PHY application note.

items.text: Magnetics center-tap connection matches the PHY type (voltage-mode or current-mode) per datasheet
items.hint: Current-mode PHYs need the center tap biased to a supply; voltage-mode PHYs typically want it AC-coupled only. Getting this wrong kills the link.

items.text: PHY reference clock (typically 25 MHz or 50 MHz) meets the PHY's frequency tolerance and jitter spec
items.hint: Check the frequency tolerance and load capacitors. In RMII, the 50 MHz clock may come from the PHY or the MAC.

items.text: MDI pairs are routed at 100 Ω differential impedance and length-matched
items.hint: Keep the pairs away from board edges and over an unbroken reference plane.

items.text: Link / activity LEDs are planned (in the jack or discrete) and their PHY strap interaction is understood
items.hint: LED pins often double as straps, so the LED circuit can set the strap level.

items.text: PHY address strapping and MDIO/MDC wiring are correct
items.hint: MDIO needs a pull-up per the PHY datasheet.

items.text: All PHY strap pins are at the intended level at reset, accounting for LED and other loads on shared pins
items.hint: Straps often share LED or MAC pins; an LED or MCU pull can flip a strap. Check the strap thresholds in the datasheet.

items.text: MAC-PHY interface mode (MII / RMII / RGMII) matches on both sides, including RGMII internal delays
items.hint: RGMII needs a clock delay inserted by the PHY, the MAC or the PCB, and by exactly one of them.

items.text: Isolation rating of the magnetics and the creepage from MDI to logic meet the product's requirement
items.hint: Check the magnetics' rated isolation voltage and keep logic copper clear of the MDI side.

items.text: PoE: PD controller classification and isolated converter are sized for the required power class
items.hint: Size the isolated DC-DC for the full class power, including efficiency and hold-up.

items.text: PoE: input TVS and bridge rectification are present per the PD controller datasheet
items.hint: A PoE PD must accept either polarity on either pair set. Check the bridge and TVS ratings per datasheet.

items.text: Antenna is matched to the module / PA output (typically 50 Ω) with a Pi or L network footprint
items.hint: Fit a Pi footprint even if only a 0 Ω is populated initially, so matching can be tuned on the final enclosure.

items.text: RF traces are impedance-controlled (e.g. 50 Ω microstrip or grounded coplanar waveguide)
items.hint: Calculate the geometry from the actual stack-up, and stitch the coplanar ground with vias.

items.text: The antenna keep-out zone is free of copper on all layers
items.hint: Follow the antenna or module vendor's keep-out drawing. Copper and components in the keep-out detune the antenna.

items.text: Crystal load capacitors for the RF device match the datasheet specification
items.hint: Frequency error directly affects radio link margin. Account for stray capacitance.

items.text: Regulatory certification route (modular approval or full certification) is decided for the end product
items.hint: A pre-certified module keeps its grant only if its conditions (antenna type, layout) are followed.

items.text: Antenna diversity or an external antenna connector option is provided if needed
items.hint: Decide this before enclosure design, since connector placement drives the mechanical layout.

items.text: Test point or U.FL-style connector is provided for conducted RF measurements
items.hint: A switched test connector or RF test pad allows conducted power and sensitivity measurements during certification.

items.text: Every GPIO has a defined state during reset and before firmware configures it
items.hint: Pins float or default to pulled states that may enable loads. Add pull resistors where a floating pin is unsafe.

items.text: Boot-mode / strap pins are at the intended level and not disturbed by attached circuits
items.hint: Check boot pins against the MCU datasheet. An external load can override the internal pull.

items.text: GPIO current per pin and per port is within MCU absolute limits
items.hint: Sum the LED and other load currents on each port against the MCU's total I/O current limit.

items.text: No input is driven above its rated voltage (5 V tolerance checked, including when the MCU is unpowered)
items.hint: 5 V-tolerant pins are often tolerant only while VDD is present.

items.text: Buttons have debounce (hardware RC or firmware) and ESD protection where user-accessible
items.hint: Use series resistance plus a TVS or ESD diode on buttons reachable through the enclosure.

items.text: Wake-capable pins are used for buttons / interrupts that must wake the device from sleep
items.hint: Not every pin can wake the MCU from its deepest sleep mode. Check the datasheet's wake-pin list.

items.text: Unused pins are configured or terminated as the MCU datasheet recommends
items.hint: Floating inputs increase supply current and can oscillate.

items.text: Debug connector pinout matches the standard probe / cable to be used
items.hint: Check pin 1 orientation and keying against the probe vendor's pinout, not just the MCU datasheet.

items.text: Target voltage reference (VTref) is connected so the probe can sense I/O voltage
items.hint: Without VTref, many probes cannot set their output levels.

items.text: Reset line is available on the debug header and has the pull-up / capacitor the MCU requires
items.hint: A large reset capacitor can stop the probe from pulling reset low quickly enough.

items.text: Debug pins are not reused for other functions in a way that blocks connection after boot
items.hint: If firmware remaps the SWD pins at boot, keep a way back in, such as connect-under-reset.

items.text: JTAG: TRST, TMS and TDI pull resistors follow the device datasheet
items.hint: Wrong pull directions can hold the TAP in reset or make the chain unreliable.

items.text: JTAG chain order and TCK fan-out are checked for multi-device chains
items.hint: Check TCK signal integrity where it fans out to several devices.

items.text: Programming access exists in production (pads, pogo-pin pattern or Tag-Connect footprint)
items.hint: Plan fixture access early. Pads hidden under components or shields cannot be probed.

items.text: Readout / debug lock plan is defined for shipped units
items.hint: Locking debug access is often irreversible. Agree the lock level and when it is applied.

items.text: Flash voltage matches the I/O supply of the controller
items.hint: Common flash parts come in 1.8 V and 3.3 V variants that share a part-number prefix.

items.text: CS has a pull-up so the flash is deselected during reset and power-up
items.hint: A floating CS can corrupt flash content during power transitions.

items.text: WP# and HOLD#/RESET# pins are pulled to an inactive state or driven when not used as IO2/IO3
items.hint: In single or dual mode these pins are control inputs and must not float.

items.text: Quad / octal mode wiring matches the flash pinout and its QE / mode configuration
items.hint: Check whether the part ships with quad mode enabled or needs a status-register write.

items.text: Boot ROM supports the chosen flash part, mode and address width if the device boots from it
items.hint: Check the boot ROM's supported command set and dummy-cycle defaults.

items.text: Flash reset is asserted with the processor reset, so the flash is not left in a 4-byte or QPI mode after a warm reset
items.hint: A warm reset that does not also reset the flash can leave the boot ROM unable to read it.

items.text: EEPROM write-protect pin is in the intended state
items.hint: Decide whether WP is controlled by firmware or strapped, and check its default level.

items.text: CMD and DAT lines have pull-ups per the SD / eMMC specification and device datasheet
items.hint: Take pull-up values from the host datasheet. Do not omit them on unused DAT lines.

items.text: CLK has series termination at the host and no pull-up
items.hint: Place the series resistor near the host to reduce ringing.

items.text: Bus lines are length-matched to CLK for the highest speed mode used
items.hint: Faster modes need tighter matching. Check the host datasheet.

items.text: UHS-I card voltage switching (3.3 V to 1.8 V signaling) is supported by the I/O supply if UHS modes are used
items.hint: Without a switchable I/O supply, the card falls back to slower modes.

items.text: SD card power is switched so the card can be power-cycled to recover from errors
items.hint: A card stuck in a bad state often recovers only after a full power cycle.

items.text: ESD protection is fitted on the user-accessible SD slot lines
items.hint: Use low-capacitance protection suited to the bus speed.

items.text: eMMC VCC and VCCQ rails and their decoupling match the device datasheet
items.hint: VCCQ may be 1.8 V or 3.3 V depending on the device and the bus mode.

items.text: DDR type, density and speed grade are supported by the controller and its boot / init software
items.hint: Confirm the controller's supported device widths, ranks and densities.

items.text: Pin and byte-lane mapping follows the controller's allowed swaps
items.hint: Many controllers allow bit swaps within a byte lane but not across lanes. Check the vendor rules.

items.text: Data byte lanes are length-matched to their strobes within the controller vendor's limits
items.hint: Use the vendor's limits, including package delays if the design guide requires them.

items.text: Address / command / control group is length-matched to the clock within the controller vendor's limits
items.hint: Fly-by and T-branch topologies have different rules. Follow the controller design guide.

items.text: VTT termination regulator can source and sink the required current (fly-by topologies)
items.hint: VTT must track VDDQ/2 and handle both sink and source current.

items.text: VREF generation, filtering and routing follow the controller / memory datasheet
items.hint: Keep VREF away from noisy nets and decouple it at each device.

items.text: ZQ calibration resistors are fitted with the specified value and tolerance
items.hint: Use a dedicated resistor per device where required; do not share ZQ resistors unless the datasheet allows it.

items.text: Memory power sequencing and RESET_n / CKE behavior follow the JEDEC device datasheet
items.hint: Incorrect sequencing can make initialization unreliable.

items.text: Signal-integrity simulation or the vendor's layout check has been completed
items.hint: Run the controller vendor's layout or SI checklist before release.

items.text: TX/RX lane polarity and lane order are correct or are supported reversals
items.hint: PCIe allows polarity inversion within a pair. Lane-reversal support depends on the device.

items.text: AC-coupling capacitors are on the TX side of each link with the value the spec requires
items.hint: Check which end of the link needs the capacitors on each pair.

items.text: Reference clock source, architecture (common / separate) and jitter meet the endpoint requirement
items.hint: Check the clock's jitter against the requirement for the PCIe generation used.

items.text: PERST# is driven with the required timing relative to power-good and refclk
items.hint: PERST# must be held asserted until power and refclk are stable.

items.text: CLKREQ# and WAKE# are wired as open-drain with pull-ups if used
items.hint: Check the pull-up voltage domain, since these signals may cross power domains.

items.text: Differential pairs are at the target impedance with intra-pair skew controlled
items.hint: Route both signals of a pair together on one reference plane, with skew compensation near the mismatch.

items.text: M.2 / card-edge connector key, pinout and power rails match the module type
items.hint: Check the M.2 key, module length and 3.3 V current per the module datasheet.

items.text: Lane count, data rate and lane mapping are supported by the processor's CSI receiver
items.hint: Check the processor supports the sensor's output format and bit depth.

items.text: D-PHY / C-PHY pairs are routed at the target impedance and length-matched to the clock lane
items.hint: Keep the clock and data lanes on the same layer and reference plane.

items.text: Sensor MCLK frequency and source match the sensor datasheet
items.hint: Some sensors need a specific MCLK frequency for their PLL to reach the configured frame rates.

items.text: Sensor power rails and sequencing match the sensor datasheet
items.hint: Image sensors often need the analog, digital and I/O rails in a specific order.

items.text: Camera control I2C (CCI) address does not clash with other devices
items.hint: Some sensors have a fixed address, so two identical cameras may need separate buses or an I2C mux.

items.text: Reset / power-down pins have defined states during processor reset
items.hint: An undefined power-down pin can leave the sensor drawing current or driving the bus while the host boots.

items.text: TMDS / main-link pairs are at the target impedance and length-matched
items.hint: Take impedance and skew limits from the transmitter / retimer design guide.

items.text: Low-capacitance ESD protection rated for the link speed is fitted at the connector
items.hint: The protection device's capacitance must suit the link speed.

items.text: DDC / AUX pull-ups and level shifting are present per the interface specification
items.hint: DDC is open-drain at 5 V on the cable side. Most SoCs need a level shifter.

items.text: Hot-plug detect is wired and level-shifted to the controller
items.hint: Hot-plug detect is often at 5 V on the cable side and needs a divider or shifter.

items.text: HDMI 5 V output has current limiting (source) or is not back-driven (sink)
items.hint: A source must limit its 5 V output; a sink must not back-drive the source through it.

items.text: DisplayPort AC-coupling capacitors are present on the main link
items.hint: Check the capacitor value and placement per the transmitter datasheet.

items.text: Transceiver ESD / surge rating suits the cable environment
items.hint: Add TVS rated for the transceiver's bus voltage range if the built-in protection is not enough. Complements the RS-232 / RS-485 checks in the UART section.

items.text: RS-485 common-mode range covers the expected ground offset between nodes, or the link is isolated
items.hint: Ground offsets between buildings or equipment can exceed the transceiver's common-mode range.

items.text: RS-485 unit load and node count are within the transceiver's rating
items.hint: Fractional unit-load transceivers allow more nodes on one segment.

items.text: Data rate and cable length are within the transceiver's slew-rate capability
items.hint: Slew-limited transceivers reduce EMI but cap the data rate.

items.text: Isolated transceivers have an isolated supply sized and laid out per datasheet
items.hint: Check the isolated supply delivers enough current for the transceiver at the maximum data rate.

items.text: RS-422 receivers are terminated and the driver remains enabled (point-to-multipoint)
items.hint: RS-422 drivers are normally always enabled. Termination sits at the far receiver.

items.text: LIN transceiver battery-pin rating covers the transients expected on the supply line
items.hint: LIN nodes connect directly to the battery line, so the transceiver sees battery transients.

items.text: Commander node has the commander pull-up and series diode per the transceiver datasheet
items.hint: Only the commander node fits the pull-up.

items.text: Bus capacitance on the node is within the transceiver / LIN spec allowance
items.hint: Excess node capacitance slows edges and can cause bit errors.

items.text: LIN wake-up and sleep modes are wired so the node meets its quiescent-current budget
items.hint: Check the node's sleep current with the transceiver in sleep mode.

items.text: ESD protection on the LIN pin is suitable for automotive-level ESD
items.hint: Choose a TVS rated for LIN bus voltages, or rely on the transceiver's rating if it is sufficient.

items.text: Transceiver INH / EN pins are wired to control the node's regulator as intended
items.hint: INH can switch the node's regulator so the node fully powers down in sleep.

items.text: Pull-up resistor value suits the bus length and number of devices
items.hint: Long buses or many devices may need a lower pull-up value. Check the device datasheet.

items.text: Strong pull-up (or external supply) is provided for devices that need it during conversion / write
items.hint: Parasitically powered devices draw extra current during temperature conversion or EEPROM writes.

items.text: Bus driver is open-drain with timing generated by a peripheral or tolerant firmware
items.hint: Bit-banged timing must survive the worst-case interrupt latency.

items.text: ESD protection is fitted where the bus leaves the board
items.hint: Use protection that does not add enough capacitance to break the bus timing.

items.text: Device discovery (ROM search) or fixed addressing is planned
items.hint: Plan how ROM codes are discovered or stored when there are several devices.

items.text: Long cable runs use a dedicated 1-Wire driver if needed
items.hint: A dedicated 1-Wire master IC handles long cable runs better than a GPIO.

items.text: 4–20 mA input: burden resistor value, tolerance and power rating suit the full current range
items.hint: Include fault currents above 20 mA and below 4 mA so faults can be detected.

items.text: 4–20 mA input: burden resistor and ADC input are protected against miswiring to the loop supply
items.hint: A field wiring error can put the loop supply directly across the burden resistor or the ADC input.

items.text: 4–20 mA loop supply compliance voltage is enough for the transmitter plus burden and cable drop
items.hint: Calculate the minimum loop supply needed at full-scale current with the worst-case cable resistance.

items.text: Thermocouple input has open-thermocouple detection (bias / burnout current)
items.hint: Without it, a broken thermocouple can read as a plausible temperature. Complements the CJC check in the ADC section.

items.text: RTD wiring (2, 3 or 4 wire) matches the lead-resistance error budget
items.hint: Two-wire RTDs add lead resistance directly to the reading; three- and four-wire connections cancel it. Complements the excitation check in the ADC section.

items.text: Bridge sensors: excitation, gain and offset are budgeted for full-scale range
items.hint: Check the bridge output range against the ADC input range at the chosen gain.

items.text: Sensor inputs have EMI filtering suited to cable length and the environment
items.hint: Use RC filtering on each input, plus differential filtering where the inputs are differential.

items.text: Codec analog supply is low-noise and decoupled per datasheet
items.hint: Analog supply noise appears directly in the audio output.

items.text: Microphone bias and input coupling capacitors are correct for the mic type
items.hint: Electret mics need a bias supply; analog MEMS mics need supply and coupling per datasheet.

items.text: Class-D amplifier output filter / ferrite choice suits the EMC requirement
items.hint: Filterless class-D outputs can radiate on long speaker wires.

items.text: Amplifier power and speaker impedance are compatible and the supply can deliver the peak current
items.hint: Peak current at low speaker impedance can sag the supply and cause resets.

items.text: Headphone output has coupling capacitors or is ground-centered (cap-less) per datasheet
items.hint: Coupling-capacitor value sets the low-frequency cutoff with the headphone impedance.

items.text: ESD protection is fitted on audio jacks without degrading audio quality
items.hint: Low-capacitance protection avoids degrading the audio quality.

items.text: Touch controller supports the sensor size and channel count
items.hint: Check the channel count and the sensor pattern against the controller vendor's guidance.

items.text: Touch controller reset line is connected and defined during processor reset
items.hint: Without reset control, a hung controller needs a full power cycle to recover.

items.text: Interrupt line is wake-capable if touch must wake the system
items.hint: Check that the interrupt pin can wake the processor from its sleep mode.

items.text: Touch supply is clean and away from display / backlight switching noise
items.hint: Display and backlight noise is a common cause of false touches.

items.text: Ground and shield connections between touch panel, display and chassis follow the vendor guidance
items.hint: Follow the touch vendor's grounding guidance; poor grounding gives false or missed touches.

items.text: Firmware / configuration file loading for the touch controller is planned
items.hint: Some controllers need a configuration or firmware file loaded at every boot.

items.text: Module footprint and keep-out follow the module vendor's reference design
items.hint: Deviating from the reference layout can affect RF performance and the module's certification.

items.text: Module supply can deliver the peak transmit current without dropping below its minimum voltage
items.hint: Cellular modules draw large current bursts; size bulk capacitance per vendor guidance.

items.text: Module reset / power-key / boot pins are controllable by the host
items.hint: Host control lets firmware recover a hung module without a full power cycle.

items.text: Host interface (UART / SPI / SDIO / USB) and its flow control are wired per the module datasheet
items.hint: Hardware flow control is usually needed at high UART rates.

items.text: Cellular: SIM / eSIM circuit has ESD protection and the required decoupling
items.hint: Check the SIM interface follows the module vendor's reference design.

items.text: GNSS: active antenna bias and LNA supply are provided if needed
items.hint: Active GNSS antennas need a DC bias on the RF feed, with a current limit to protect against a shorted cable.

items.text: Module certifications cover the chosen antenna type and gain
items.hint: Using a different antenna type or a higher gain can invalidate the module's certification.

items.text: Driver enable / PWM inputs are pulled to a safe (off) state during MCU reset
items.hint: Use pull resistors on driver inputs so the bridge stays off before firmware runs. Complements the dead-time and break-input checks in Timers & PWM.

items.text: Current sense feedback scaling and filtering suit the ADC range and the control loop
items.hint: Check the sense amplifier's bandwidth and the filter delay against the control loop requirement.

items.text: Driver fault output is wired to an interrupt or the timer break input
items.hint: Route the fault to the timer break input so the outputs shut down in hardware.

items.text: Hall / encoder inputs have filtering and pull-ups for the cable length
items.hint: Long cables near motor wiring pick up noise; add filtering and pull-ups at the receiver.

items.text: Driver SPI / configuration interface is at a compatible logic level
items.hint: Some drivers have 5 V logic levels that need translation to 3.3 V MCUs.

items.text: Logic ground and power ground are joined so that motor currents do not flow in the logic reference
items.hint: Motor current through the logic ground shifts logic references and causes false readings.

items.text: 24 V digital inputs tolerate reverse polarity and the overvoltage expected in the installation
items.hint: Field wiring errors and surges are common in industrial installations.

items.text: Input thresholds and current match the relevant input type (e.g. IEC 61131-2 type 1 / 3) where required
items.hint: Industrial input types define switching thresholds and minimum currents for compatibility with sensors.

items.text: Inputs are isolated or filtered so field noise does not reach logic
items.hint: Optocouplers or digital isolators keep field noise and ground offsets out of the logic.

items.text: High-side outputs have short-circuit and thermal protection
items.hint: Use smart high-side switches with built-in protection, or discrete current limiting.

items.text: Inductive loads on outputs have a demagnetization / clamp path
items.hint: Turning off an inductive load without a clamp path can destroy the output switch.

items.text: Surge and EFT protection on field terminals suits the target immunity level
items.hint: Choose TVS and filtering suited to the expected surge and EFT levels.

items.text: Field-side supply is protected and fused
items.hint: Protect the field supply with a fuse or electronic current limit so a field short does not take down the board.
